chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

Regarding the man who slanders his wife: he is whipped, then they are separated, and he is not subjected to li'an (mutual cursing) until he says that he has seen someone committing immorality with her between her two legs.

key_terms.يَقْذِفُ: to slander or accuse of adultery
key_terms.يُلَاعِنُهَا: he performs li'an (mutual cursing) with her

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between li'an and the punishment for slandering one's wife in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies a specific legal nuance in Shia jurisprudence regarding *li'an* (oath of imprecation), distinguishing between a general accusation and one supported by the claim of witnessing a third party. It highlights the procedural shift where the husband is flogged and separated without the full four-oath ritual, reflecting the Imams' emphasis on evidentiary precision in marital disputes. This ruling underscores the balance between preserving marital bonds and enforcing accountability for false accusations in the absence of the required four witnesses.
